build.evidence: The dirty tree was TASK-2-09's click emission, which landed minutes later as 0a91ca959d138ae6f4c8e5e9e961d5e103db4400. Measuring without it would have recorded a number the shipped redirect cannot meet. Rebuilding the image from the committed tree reproduced the runtime stage's `COPY --from=build /repo/apps/api/dist` from cache, so the artifact under load is byte-identical to the one that commit builds; across every path the Dockerfile copies, the two trees differ by one character inside apps/api/src/clicks/click-event-buffer.spec.ts, which no bundle imports.

targetP99Basis: ceil(measured p99 2.850 ms x 2) = 6. Measured at 500 RPS for 60 s against the local docker compose stack on the machine above, NOT against a deployed instance with a managed cache: ADR-0030 chose no deploy target, so ADR-0018's layer 2 has nothing to run against. The server-side number includes the cache round trip, so a managed cache moves it materially. The ADR that supersedes ADR-0030 re-derives this from a layer-2 run before it is quoted as a promise. It is <= 25, so AC-62 holds either way. See docs/performance/redirect-baseline.md.
ciP99BudgetBasis: PROVISIONAL. ciMeasuredP99 is null because the performance job has never run: no measurement from ubuntu-latest exists. Derived as ceil(worst of three local 100 RPS runs, 3.754 ms, x 5) = 19, where the x5 stands for a slower shared four-vCPU runner and is the only unmeasured figure in this baseline. THE FIRST GREEN performance JOB IS THE CALIBRATION: set ciMeasuredP99 to the median serverP99 it prints, set ciP99BudgetMs to ceil(worst of its three runs x 2), and record the run in docs/performance/redirect-baseline.md. A tripwire, never a latency commitment.
